The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik

Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed seeking the following relief:
"...may be pleased:
i. To issue a Writ of Mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order, or direction quashing and setting aside the Impugned Suspension Letter dated 14.10.2024 (filed as Exhibit P-6), issued by the Respondent.
ii. Direct the respondents to consider the bids of Petitioner in ongoing including future tender processes of Respondent.
iii. to pass..."

2. Heard Sri Sivaraju Srinivas, learned Senior Counsel, representing Sri Harshavardhan Abburi,
learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S. Srikant, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent Corporation.
3.

Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner Company, having been registered under the Companies Act, 2013, vide Certificate of Incorporation dated 23.01.2018, is engaged in the business of building installation, including the activities performed at the site of construction, and it has been successfully executing projects, with a proven track record of its executed projects and towards adherence to contractual obligations, demonstrating its commitment to PK, J quality and client satisfaction.

It was further submitted that respondent No.1 issued a Tender notification bearing No.NIT/BID/Ref.No.EEF:/06/ 24-25/SERC Conts/SLNP/TS/67ULV/
Disc/R&M/OTE-242501 dated 22.04.2024, for dismantling, installation, commissioning for 40,194 numbers of LED streetlights and the repair and maintenance of 1,33,134 numbers of LED streetlights for a period of five years or till the project completion of respective Urban Local Body and other related works in sixty seven Urban Local Bodies project in the State of Telangana.

In pursuance thereof, the petitioner Company submitted its bid on 14.05.2024, in strict compliance with the terms and conditions stipulated in the Tender Notification, and while the evaluation process of the tender was going on, the petitioner Company had received an e-mail from respondent No.1 on 16.08.2024, requesting to fill in the Bill of Material (BOM) Form and to submit the same by 05:00 PM on 17.08.2024.
Thereafter, a reminder e-mail dated 17.08.2024 was received by the petitioner seeking to submit the said BOM Form.

In response, the petitioner, initially vide e-mail dated 17.08.2024, informed that the concerned Executive Authority in the petitioner Company was unavailable, and thus, sought for extension of time for submitting the BOM Form till 20.08.2024.

It was further submitted that the petitioner, vide e-mail dated 23.08.2024, had informed the respondent Corporation PK, J that it had chosen to withdraw from the tender process, considering Vinci Global Private Limited vs Energy Efficiency Services Limited on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64666655/
1 its financial situation and budgets.

sentences.text: However, to the utter shock and surprise of the petitioner, after more than forty-five days, the impugned order dated 14.10.2024 was passed, indicating that the petitioner Company has been suspended from participating in the tendering process of the EESL Tenders for a period of one year.

4. Learned Senior Counsel contended that the petitioner had withdrawn from the Tender process even before it was declared as L1 bidder and the respondents also never informed the petitioner Company that it was declared as a successful bidder/L1 bidder, and they had also failed to appraise the petitioner Company about the opening of technical and financial bids, which was followed in another tender floated by the very same respondent.

Further, the petitioner Company was not even issued with the Letter of Award of Tender, and the respondents, on no occasion, responded to the e-mail dated 23.08.2024 sent by the petitioner, by informing that it has been qualified as a successful/L1 bidder, so it cannot backout as per the terms and conditions of the tender notification.

It was further submitted that the petitioner Company was issued with a Letter of Award dated 14.03.2024, which pertains to another tender floated by the respondent for design, manufacturing,
supply, testing and commissioning of CCMs with up to PK, J seven years comprehensive warranty on site (including supply of spare parts on site during warranty period) with Repair and Maintenance until the warranty period of 22,135 numbers of CCMs on PAN India basis.
In the said tender, the respondents followed the procedure determined under the respective RFP and intimated the opening of the First Envelope and Second Envelope and awarded the tender accordingly.

However, in the present tender, the respondents failed to communicate the petitioner Company on the opening of its bids, including that of qualifying the petitioner Company as L1 bidder and they only sought a clarification on BOM Form.
Thus, the respondents cannot take alternative approach in different tenders and act arbitrarily.

5. It was further contended that the respondents had never issued any show-cause notice seeking any clarification from the petitioner as to why it should not be kept under holiday list as per the terms of the Tender Notification, and issued the impugned order dated 14.10.2024, erroneously placing the petitioner under holiday list for a period of one year from participating in the tenders of the respondents, without affording any opportunity to the petitioner to present its case or provide any explanation for withdrawal of its bid or provide any explanation to the contemplated the action of the respondents, thereby, depriving the petitioner of its fundamental right of being heard.

As such, the PK, J unilateral action of the respondents is blatantly arbitrary, unfair and is in complete violation of principles of natural justice, fundamental rights and terms of the tender notification.

It was further submitted that the petitioner made a representation to the respondents on 16.10.2024,
requesting to set aside the impugned suspension order.
However, no action has been taken so far.

6. It was further submitted that the action of the respondents in placing the petitioner Company under holiday list and suspending it from participating in tendering process of the respondents'
tenders for a period of one year tantamount to blacklisting, and such a blacklisting without issuance of a show-cause notice or providing an opportunity of being heard is in utter violation of principles of natural justice.

Further, in view of the impugned action of the respondents, the petitioner Company has is under a threat of termination of contracts of other authorities or contractors working with the petitioner, on the alleged suspension and holiday listing/blacklisting.

It was also submitted that the withdrawal of the petitioner's bid did not cause PK, J any financial loss or prejudice to the respondents as the petitioner withdrew its bid even before the finalization and declaration of L1 bidder.

However, in spite of the same, the respondents imposed a disproportionate and unjust punishment on the petitioner by suspending and holiday listing it for a period of two years, which is not only detrimental to the petitioner's business interests but also sets a dangerous precedent for future tender inviting authorities to consider the bid of the petitioner Company.
As such, the action of the respondents is a clear manifestation of its arbitrary abuse of power, causing irreparable damage to the petitioner's reputation and its business prospects.
Therefore, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner prayed this Court to allow the writ petition by setting aside the impugned order dated 14.10.2024.

Reliance has been placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in UMC Technologies Private Limited v. Food Corporation of India 1.

The petitioner participated in the said Tender and its First Envelope (Technical Bid) was opened on 14.05.2024 at 11:30 hours and the Second Envelope (Price Bid) was opened on 13.08.2024, after notifying the bidders vide an automated e-mail dated 13.08.2024, through the Tender Wizard Portal.

The prices quoted by the petitioner and other bidders were transparently displayed on the Tender Wizard Portal, which, the petitioner was also fully aware of, as the petitioner is a regular participant in the tenders floated by respondent No.1 and it is known that the entire tendering process is conducted transparently online.

8. Subsequently, respondent No.1 conducted evaluation of bids, and found the petitioner as L1 in all the three quoted clusters since the total contract price quoted by the petitioner was abnormally low compared to others.

As such, respondent No.1 sent an e-mail dated 16.08.2024, seeking justification from the petitioner through submission of a Bill of Materials (BOM) Form to ascertain the viability of the quoted price and PK, J before the expiry of timeline of 17:00 hours on 17.08.2024, a gentle reminder was also given to the petitioner.

sentences.text: The prolonged absence of adequate lighting has raised safety concerns, disrupted daily activities and led to increased complaints from residents and local authorities.

Further, this delay has resulted in financial and operational losses for respondent No.1, including increased project management costs,
potential penalties and PK, J reputational damage.
The cash flows from ULBs have also been adversely affected, as expected revenues from the project implementation and operations have been delayed.

9. It was further submitted that after thorough examination of the replies of the petitioner dated 17.08.2024 and 23.08.2024, the competent authority came to a conclusion that the reasons for withdrawal from the Tender are cryptic and that the petitioner had no rationale behind its withdrawal, as it was fully aware of its financial implications in the event of award of Tender to the petitioner.

Since the decision of the petitioner to back out from the Tender lacks proper reasoning and any basis whatsoever, the benefit of principles of natural justice cannot be accorded to such erring/defaulting parties.

The petitioner was found to be in breach of the tender conditions and as per the RFP/Tender conditions, if the L1 bidder backs out, then the bidder will be put on holiday list of the respondent Company for a period of one year, during which period, the bidder will be barred from participating in the tenders floated by the respondent Company.

As such, respondent No.1 is justified in issuing the impugned order dated 14.10.2024, in accordance with the RFP conditions,
more particularly, Clause 16 of Part-C of Section 4 of the Tender notification.
Therefore, it was prayed to dismiss the present writ petition.

Admittedly, the petitioner participated in a tender floated by the respondent Corporation vide No.NIT/BID/Ref.No.EEF:/06/ 24-25/SERC Conts/SLNP/TS/67ULV/ Disc/R&M/OTE-242501 dated 22.04.2024, for dismantling, installation, commissioning for 40,194 numbers of LED streetlights and the repair and maintenance of 1,33,134 numbers of LED streetlights, for a period of five years or till the project completion of respective Urban Local Body and other related works in sixty seven Urban Local Bodies project in the State of Telangana.

sentences.text: In this connection, it is relevant to refer to Clause 16 of Part-C of Section 4 of the Tender notification, which deals with the action to be taken by the Company if L1 bidder back out.

The said clause is extracted hereunder:
"Part-C-Technical Specifications of Section 4:
16. Action by ESSL,

if L1 backs out After opening of price bid, if L1 bidder backs out,
the bidder will be put on holiday list of EESL for a period of one year.
During this tenure, the bidder will be barred from participation in EESL tendering process.
However, bidder has to continue the unexecuted work of the other prevailing work if any under the current running contracts.
Simultaneously, the EMD submitted by such bidder against the subject tender will be forfeited.
If the Bidder is exempted from submission of EMD, then the EMD amount will be adjusted from the payments due to the contractor against other running contracts.

If there is no running contract of the bidder/no payment dues to the bidder, then EESL reserves the right to take any legal remedy as deemed fit to recover the penalty equivalent to EMD amount through legal means."
13. It is thus clear from the above that an L1 bidder will be placed under holiday list of the respondent Company, if it backs out/withdraws from the tendering process, after opening the bid.

However, in the PK, J instant case, although the respondents assert that the petitioner was declared as L1 bidder as per their internal evaluation, it is to be noted that before the withdrawal of the petitioner's bid, no Letter of Award of Tender was issued nor was any communication was sent to the petitioner, declaring it as L1 bidder.
As such, respondent No.1 ought not to have invoked this Clause and passed the impugned order placing the petitioner under holiday list.

Further, according to respondent No.1, only the L1 bidders are requested to furnish the Bill of Material Form, but it is its obligation to communicate the L1 status to the respective bidder for proceeding with the contract.
However, no material has been placed on record to show that there was any communication between the parties with regard to declaring the petitioner as L1 bidder.
14. Further, the petitioner contended that no notice was issued before passing the impugned order nor was any opportunity granted to it to submit its case.
However, no counter arguments are presented in this regard to rebut this contention of the petitioner.
As such, it can be inferred that the impugned order was issued in clear violation of the principles of natural justice, without affording an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.

15. In this regard, it is pertinent to note that the Hon'ble Apex Court, time and again, held that even in contractual matters, any order that PK, J has civil consequences should only be passed after following the principles of natural justice, duly affording an opportunity of hearing.

In a catena of judgments, it was also categorically held that the consequences of blacklisting are substantively severe as it not only bars a company from participating in the Government Tenders, but also casts a stigma upon it, affecting its business reputation with other clients.

sentences.text:
In Erusian Equipment & Chemicals Ltd. v. State of West Bengal 5, the Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
12. Under Article 298 of the Constitution the executive power of the Union and the State shall extend to the carrying on of any trade and to the acquisition, holding and disposal of property and the making of contracts for any purpose.

entities.text: Erusian Equipment & Chemicals Ltd. v. State of West Bengal 5

sentences.text: The State can carry on executive function by making a law or without making a law.
The exercise of such powers and functions in trade by the State is subject to Part III of the Constitution.
Article 14 speaks of equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.
Equality of opportunity should apply to matters of public contracts.
The State has the right to trade.
The State has there the duty to observe equality.
An ordinary individual can choose not to deal with any person.
The Government cannot choose to exclude persons by discrimination.
The order of blacklisting has the effect of depriving a person of equality of opportunity in the matter of public contract.
A person who is on the approved list is unable to enter into advantageous relations with the Government because of the order of blacklisting.
A person who has been dealing with the Government in the matter of sale and purchase of materials has a legitimate interest or expectation.
When the State acts to the prejudice of a person it has to be supported by legality.
The blacklisting order does not pertain to any particular contract.
The blacklisting order involves civil consequences.
It casts a slur.
It creates a barrier between the persons blacklisted and the Government in the matter of transactions.
The blacklists are "instruments of coercion".

... 
20. Blacklisting has the effect of preventing a person from the privilege and advantage of entering into lawful relationship with the Government for purposes of gains.
The fact that a disability is created by the order of blacklisting indicates that the relevant authority is to have an objective satisfaction.

Fundamentals of fair play require that the person concerned should be given an opportunity to represent his case before he is put on the blacklist."
17.

In Gorkha Security Services v. Government (NCT of Delhi) and others 6, while emphasizing the necessity of a show-cause notice, the Hon'ble Apex Court, described blacklisting as equivalent to civil death.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court are extracted hereunder:
"16. It is a common case of the parties that the blacklisting has to be preceded by a show-cause notice.
Law in this regard is firmly grounded and does not even demand much amplification.

The necessity of compliance with the principles of natural justice by giving the opportunity to the person against whom action of blacklisting is sought Vinci Global Private Limited vs Energy Efficiency Services Limited on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64666655/
6 to be taken has a valid and solid rationale behind it.

entities.text: Vinci Global Private Limited vs Energy Efficiency Services Limited on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With blacklisting, many civil and/or evil consequences follow.

It is described as "civil death"
of a person who is foisted with the order of blacklisting.
Such an order is stigmatic in nature and debars such a person from participating in government tenders which means precluding him from the award of government contracts.
The central issue, however, pertains to the requirement of stating the action which is proposed to be taken.
The fundamental purpose behind the serving of show-cause notice is to make the noticee understand the precise case set up against him which he has to meet.
This would require the statement of imputations detailing out the alleged breaches and defaults he has committed, so that he gets an opportunity to rebut the same.
Another requirement, according to us, is the nature of action which is proposed to be taken for such a breach.

That should also be stated so that the noticee is able to point out that proposed action is not warranted in the given case, even if the defaults/breaches complained of are not satisfactorily explained.

When it comes to blacklisting, this requirement becomes all the more imperative, having regard to the fact that it is harshest possible action."
18.
In UMC Technologies Pvt. Ltd. (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court made the following observations:

"13. At the outset, it must be noted that it is the first principle of civilised jurisprudence that a person against whom any action is sought to be taken or whose right or interests are being affected should be given a reasonable opportunity to defend himself.
The basic principle of natural justice is that before adjudication starts, the authority concerned should give to the affected party a notice of the case against him so that he can defend himself.
Such notice should be adequate and the grounds necessitating action and the penalty/action proposed should be mentioned specifically and unambiguously.
An order travelling beyond the bounds of notice is impermissible and without jurisdiction to that extent.

This Court in Nasir Ahmad v.
Custodian General, Evacuee Property [Nasir Ahmad v. Custodian General, Evacuee Property, (1980) 3 SCC 1] has held that it is essential for the notice to specify the particular grounds on the basis of which an action is proposed to be taken so as to enable the noticee to answer the case against him.

Nasir Ahmad v.
Custodian General, Evacuee Property [Nasir Ahmad v. Custodian General, Evacuee Property, (1980) 3 SCC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If these conditions are not satisfied, the person cannot be said to have been granted any reasonable opportunity of being heard.

14. Specifically, in the context of blacklisting of a person or an entity by the State or a State Corporation, the requirement of a valid, particularised and unambiguous show-cause notice is PK, J particularly crucial due to the severe consequences of Vinci Global Private Limited vs Energy Efficiency Services Limited on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64666655/
7 blacklisting and the stigmatisation that accrues to the person/entity being blacklisted.

entities.text: Vinci Global Private Limited vs Energy Efficiency Services Limited on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Here, it may be gainful to describe the concept of blacklisting and the graveness of the consequences occasioned by it.
Blacklisting has the effect of denying a person or an entity the privileged opportunity of entering into government contracts.

This privilege arises because it is the State who is the counterparty in government contracts and as such, every eligible person is to be afforded an equal opportunity to participate in such contracts, without arbitrariness and discrimination.
Not only does blacklisting take away this privilege, it also tarnishes the blacklisted person's reputation and brings the person's character into question.
Blacklisting also has long-lasting civil consequences for the future business prospects of the blacklisted person.

... 
19. In light of the above decisions, it is clear that a prior show- cause notice granting a reasonable opportunity of being heard is an essential element of all administrative decision-making and particularly so in decisions pertaining to blacklisting which entail grave consequences for the entity being blacklisted.

In these cases, furnishing of a valid show-cause notice is critical and a failure to do so would be fatal to any order of blacklisting pursuant thereto."
19.

As regards all the decisions relied on by the respondents, the Hon'ble Apex Court, categorically held that the power of judicial review in matters of government contracts and tenders is limited, and that the Courts should not ordinarily interfere with the evaluation process or the terms and conditions of a tender.
However, the said decisions are of no avail to the respondents as the present case involves a grave violation of principles of natural justice.
PK, J 20.

In the light of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the impugned order dated 14.10.2024 is unsustainable in the eye of law, and is, therefore, liable to be set aside.

21. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed setting aside the impugned order vide letter bearing reference No.EESL/05/2024- 25/SERC-CONTRACTS/SLNP-TG/Suspension/001 dated 14.10.2024 issued by respondent No.1.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this writ petition, shall stand closed.
No costs.
